In [[cryptography]], '''xmx''' is a [[block cipher]] designed in 1997 by David
M'Raïhi, [[David Naccache]], [[Jacques Stern (cryptographer)|Jacques Stern]], and [[Serge Vaudenay]]. According to the
designers it "uses [[public-key cryptography|public-key]]-like operations as [[confusion and diffusion]] means." The
cipher was designed for efficiency, and the only operations it uses are [[XOR]]s
and [[modular arithmetic|modular multiplications]].

The main parameters of xmx are variable, including the
[[block size (cryptography)|block size]] and [[key size]], which are equal, as well
as the number of rounds. In addition to the [[key (cryptography)|key]], it also makes
use of an odd modulus ''n'' which is small enough to fit in a single block.

The round function is f(m)=(m<small>o</small>a)·b mod n, where a and b are
subkeys and b is [[coprime]] to n. Here m<small>o</small>a represents an operation that
equals m XOR a, if that is less than n, and otherwise equals m. This is a simple
invertible operation: m<small>o</small>a<small>o</small>a = m. The xmx cipher consists
of an even number of iterations of the round function, followed by a final <small>o</small>
with an additional subkey.

The [[key schedule]] is very simple, using the same key for all the multipliers, and
three different subkeys for the others: the key itself for the first half of the
cipher, its [[multiplicative inverse]] mod n for the last half, and the XOR of these two
for the middle subkey.

The designers defined four specific variants of xmx:
* ''Standard'': 512-bit block size, 8 rounds, n=2<sup>512</sup>-1
* ''High security'': 768-bit block size, 12 rounds, n=2<sup>768</sup>-1
* ''Very-high security'': 1024-bit block size, 16 rounds, n=2<sup>1024</sup>-1
* ''Challenge'': 256-bit block size, 8 rounds, n=(2<sup>80</sup>-1)·2<sup>176</sup>+157

Borisov, et al., using a multiplicative form of [[differential cryptanalysis]], found a
complementation property for any variant of xmx, like the first three above, such that
n=2<sup>k</sup>-1, where k is the block size. They also found large [[weak key]] classes
for the Challenge variant, and for many other moduli.
